newsitem.title: USA: NBC buys stake in Cablevision's Rainbow.
newsitem.headline: NBC buys stake in Cablevision's Rainbow.

text.p: General Electric Co's NBC television network said on Monday it has acquired a 25 percent equity interest in Cablevision Systems Corp's Rainbow Programming Holdings Inc, which gives it a stake in Madison Square Garden properties.
Terms of the agreement were not disclosed. The companies could not be reached immediately for comment.

The move came a week after reports that Cablevision was pursuing several debt-reduction plans, including lining up a strategic financial partner for all or part of its cable and programming operations.
NBC already had a stake in Rainbow networks. The companies said that under certain unspecified circumstances, NBC's stake in Rainbow could grow to 27 percent.

Earlier this month, ITT Corp, which is fending off a hostile takeover bid from Hilton Hotels Corp, said it would sell its half interest in Madison Square Garden to Cablevision, its partner, for $650 million.

As a result of the deal between NBC and Rainbow, NBC would now have a stake in the Garden properties, which include MSG Network, the New York Knicks basketball team and the New York Rangers hockey team.

NBC spokeswoman Lela Cocoros said later Monday that NBC did not have to spend any money to convert its stake in Rainbow networks, such as American Movie Classics and Bravo, to a 25 percent equity interest in the company.
"No money has exchanged hands," Cocoros said.

Rainbow President and Chief Executive Joshua Sapan said later Monday that although no money was involved in the deal, the partnership with NBC could "clear the path" for such arrangements in the future.
If Cablevision or Rainbow "chose to take in a strategic partner, that's a simpler thing to accomplish" under the new relationship, he said.
